edits.oldText:
Move overload-set construction into OverloadSetOracle

Do not immediately delete synthetic property lookup behavior. Instead, make it delegate to the oracle first.

ETSObjectType::CreateSyntheticVarFromEverySignature(...) {
    auto set = checker->SemanticRelations().Overloads().GetOverloadSet(...);
    return CreateSyntheticFunctionTypeFrom(set);
}

This lets existing call sites keep working while overload set formation becomes centralized, cached, and testable.
edits.newText:
Move method overload-set construction behind shared queries

Do not immediately delete synthetic property lookup behavior. Instead, make it delegate to the shared relation component first.

ETSObjectType::CreateSyntheticVarFromEverySignature(...) {
    auto set = checker->SemanticRelations().GetMethodOverloadSet(...);
    return CreateSyntheticFunctionTypeFrom(set);
}

This lets existing call sites keep working while method overload set formation becomes centralized, cached, and testable.

edits.oldText:
Migrate override consumers to OverrideOracle

No permanent override state is required. Each validation pass asks the oracle the exhaustive questions it needs; the oracle caches answers.
edits.newText:
Migrate override consumers to shared override queries

No permanent override state is required. Each validation pass asks the shared relation component the exhaustive questions it needs; the component caches answers.

edits.oldText: After interface validation uses OverrideOracle, add one default-method resolution path and make checker diagnostics agree with emitted/default-forwarding representation.
edits.newText: After interface validation uses shared override queries, add one default-method resolution path and make checker diagnostics agree with emitted/default-forwarding representation.

edits.oldText:
Atomic switch to single bridge planning

Once OverrideOracle consumers are stable, bridge planning should stop rediscovering overrides in both current bridge phases and query GetOverriddenTargets instead.

  • Disable semantic bridge rediscovery in CreateGenericBridges and CreateOverrideBridges in the same patch.
  • Generate bridge plans from oracle targets.
  • Treat generic-substitution and override-conversion needs as reasons on the same target.
  • Deduplicate by effective/assembly descriptor.
  • Reuse bridge body builders where possible.
  • Add runtime dispatch tests for generated bridges.

Running old generic/override rediscovery and new bridge planning together risks duplicate bridge methods or inconsistent signatures.
edits.newText:
Bridge phases consume shared target discovery

Once shared override queries are stable, bridge planning should stop rediscovering overrides independently and query shared overridden-target discovery instead.

  • Both current bridge phases may remain physically separate at first.
  • They should consume the same overridden-target facts.
  • Treat generic-substitution and override-conversion needs as reasons on the same target.
  • Deduplicate by effective/assembly descriptor.
  • Reuse bridge body builders where possible.
  • Add runtime dispatch tests for generated bridges.

Running old semantic rediscovery beside new target discovery risks duplicate bridge methods or inconsistent signatures; physical phase unification is optional, but shared semantics are not.

content.text:
Finding #1

No single source of truth for overriding

The same semantic relation — “derived method X overrides base method Y” — is calculated in several places for different purposes. That creates divergence risk.

Current style

  • Method checker decides some override facts.
  • Interface checker separately compares interface methods.
  • Generic and override bridge phases scan supertypes again.
  • Overload collection suppresses candidates with its own logic.

Consequence

  • Diagnostics and bridge generation can disagree.
  • Multiple-interface cases are fragile.
  • Hard to reason about one method overriding several inherited methods.
  • Hard to detect duplicate override-of-same-base uniformly.

The checker should compute override edges once and make every consumer use them.

Finding #2 status

Default-interface conflict should respect concrete class implementation

Status: active compiler deficiency. A concrete class/superclass method that implements an interface method should suppress conflicts between inherited defaults for that same method.

class C1 { foo(): string { return "" } }
interface I1 { foo(): string { return "1" } }
interface I2 { foo(): string { return "2" } }
class C2 extends C1 implements I1, I2 {}

Expected

C2 inherits C1.foo; that method implements both interface methods, so no default conflict remains.

Fix direction

Before reporting a default-method conflict, query HasCommonConcreteImplementation; in the full design this becomes part of method implementation resolution.

Keep the abstract-interface variant as regression coverage, but it is not the active Finding #2 issue.

Finding #3

Overload-equivalence is not cleanly implemented

Current logic around duplicate overloads mixes several concepts: signature identity, return type, assembly descriptor collision, and helper overload generation. This is dangerous because the spec has a simpler source-level rule.

Language-level question

Are these two declarations illegally overload-equivalent in source?

same parameter count
same effective parameter types
ignore return type

ABI-level question

Will these two methods collide in generated descriptors or require helper/bridge methods?

assembly type descriptors
possibly include return
backend/runtime constraints

These questions should not be answered by the same helper.

Finding #4

Effective signature type is not explicit

The spec gives effective type mapping rules. The implementation needs an actual helper that represents this mapping, otherwise the checker will keep using approximations such as ordinary subtyping or assembler type strings.

Type *EffectiveType(Type *type);
Type *EffectiveSignatureType(Type *type);

Target

  • One oracle-driven bridge planning path.
  • Lowering queries GetOverriddenTargets.
  • NeedsBridge decides descriptor/adaptation needs.
  • Existing body builders can be reused mechanically.
Updated target design

Stateless, lazy semantic relation services

The updated approach does not store permanent override relation data on AST nodes or object types. Instead, the checker owns short-lived relation services that recompute facts lazily and are explicitly cleared on Recheck and plugin mutation barriers.

1. OverrideOracle

Answers questions such as “does this method override that one?” and “which inherited targets does this method override?”

2. OverloadSetOracle

Builds ordered overload candidate sets on demand, including explicit overload expansion and inherited candidate suppression.

3. Implementation resolver

Selects concrete or interface-default implementations and removes overridden defaults before emission planning.

4. Resolved call target

Stores the selected function/method/constructor target on each call so lowering does not redo semantic discovery.

Override information is exposed as lazy cached relation queries, not as a stored data structure on AST/type nodes.

Updated target design

SemanticRelationCache

class SemanticRelationCache {
public:
    void Clear();

    OverrideOracle &Overrides();
    OverloadSetOracle &Overloads();
    MethodImplementationResolver &Implementations();
    GenericViewResolver &GenericViews();

private:
    OverrideOracle overrideOracle_;
    OverloadSetOracle overloadOracle_;
    MethodImplementationResolver implementationResolver_;
    GenericViewResolver genericViewResolver_;
};
  • Owned by ETSChecker.
  • Caches are cleared during safe Recheck and after plugin mutation barriers.
  • No epoch is required for the short-term design if cache lifetime is strictly tied to checker runs and explicit clearing.
  • An epoch/generation counter can be added later as a debug guard or for fine-grained LSP/plugin incremental invalidation.
  • This is similar in spirit to TypeRelation: relation answers are cached, but not permanently stored on every AST/type node.

- treat generic-substitution bridges and override-conversion bridges as reasons attached to the same override target, not as separate hierarchy searches;
- deduplicate by effective/assembly descriptor;
- preserve existing bridge body generation helpers where possible.

This should be one patch to avoid duplicate or missing bridges. The final code may keep small helper builders split by bridge body shape, but there should be only one semantic bridge discovery/planning path.

## Phase 11: cleanup

After migration:

- reduce overload-specific property lookup flags;
- remove or shrink synthetic overload variable construction in `GetProperty`;
- remove duplicated override predicates;
- remove casual `CallSignatures().front()` in overload paths;
- make call resolution consume overload sets directly from the oracle.

---

## What can be done gradually

Safe gradual changes:

1. Add characterization tests.
2. Classify suppressed overriding failures by owning semantic service.
3. Add pure helper functions.
4. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision.
5. Add effective signature type helper.
6. Introduce one checker-owned `SemanticRelations`/`SemanticRelationCache` component with delegated query helpers.
7. Move method overload-set construction behind the shared relation component where currently needed.
8. Move override diagnostics and interface validation behind shared override queries.
9. Add method implementation resolution behind the same relation component.
10. Remove duplicate predicates after relation consumers are stable.

---

## What should be done all at once

Some changes must be atomic because partial migration would create inconsistent semantics.

| Change | Why it should be atomic |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit overload expansion | Validation, synthetic type construction, call resolution, and lowering must agree about candidate count/order. |
| Resolved call target representation | Checker and lowering must switch together from owner-variable assumptions to explicit target metadata. |
| Single oracle-driven bridge planning | Running old generic/override rediscovery and new oracle-driven planning together risks duplicate or missing bridges. |
| Default-method emission switch | Checker implementation-resolution results and emitted/default-forwarding representation must agree, otherwise verifier/linker can still see multiple defaults. |
| Direct overload-set call resolution | `MemberExpression`, `CallExpression`, method references, explicit overloads, and lowering must agree. |
| Effective overload-equivalence across declaration kinds | Functions, methods, interfaces, and constructors must use the same language rule. |

---

## Recommended implementation order

1. Add characterization tests and classify suppressed overriding failures by semantic service.
2. Add pure override compatibility and overload-equivalence helpers.
3. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision checks.
4. Implement effective signature type and use it for overload-equivalence.
5. Add checker-owned `SemanticRelations`/`SemanticRelationCache` with coarse cache clearing; conceptual `OverrideOracle`, `OverloadSetOracle`, method implementation, and generic-view query groups can be implemented as methods/helpers first.
6. Add generic view/substitution support for inherited signatures used by shared relation queries.
7. Implement explicit overload expansion as an atomic patch.
8. Move method overload-set construction into the shared relation component behind existing APIs where currently needed.
9. Migrate interface implementation/conflict checks to shared override and implementation-resolution queries.
10. Add verifier-safe selected-default emission based on implementation-resolution results.
11. Migrate overload-set duplicate suppression to shared override-target queries.
12. Make bridge phases consume shared override-target discovery/dedup; physical bridge-phase unification is optional initially.
13. Remove obsolete synthetic/ad-hoc overload paths.

content.text:
The current frontend has pieces, but not one model

The current implementation is not empty or naive. It already parses explicit overload declarations, groups same-name methods, resolves calls by scanning signatures, validates many override cases, and creates bridge methods. The problem is that these pieces are not coordinated by one semantic representation.

Works for many simple cases

Simple same-name methods, ordinary class overrides, and many direct method calls are already handled.

Fragile for hard cases

Multiple interfaces, inherited explicit overload aliases, erasure collisions, and bridge requirements are handled by separate mechanisms that can disagree.

Needed end state

The checker should provide one semantic relation service for override queries and overload sets. Lowering should consume those answers, not rediscover them.

Key idea: use stateless, lazy, TypeRelation-inspired services with per-checker-run caches: OverrideOracle, OverloadSetOracle, method implementation resolution, and explicit resolved call targets.

## Lowering

Relevant files:

- `compiler/lowering/ets/overloadMappingLowering.cpp`
- `compiler/lowering/ets/genericBridgesLowering.cpp`
- `compiler/lowering/ets/overrideBridgesLowering.cpp`

`OverloadMappingLowering` rewrites calls to explicit overload aliases to the selected real method name.

Current bridge generation is split into two physical lowering phases:

- `GenericBridgesPhase` / `CreateGenericBridges` in `genericBridgesLowering.cpp`;
- `OverrideBridgesPhase` / `CreateOverrideBridges` in `overrideBridgesLowering.cpp`.

Both phases can reason about inherited methods and generated bridge descriptors. This is a correctness risk because generic substitution bridges and override-conversion bridges are not independent semantic domains; they are two reasons why the same source-level override relation may need a runtime adapter.

  • Owned by ETSChecker.
  • Caches are cleared during safe Recheck and after plugin mutation barriers.
    • [958 more lines in file. Use offset=786 to continue.]

The service names are design vocabulary. The implementation can start as one internal SemanticRelations component with shared helpers and caches.

class SemanticRelations {
public:
    Signature *ViewSignature(...);
    OverrideDecision IsOverride(const MethodView &base,
                                const MethodView &derived);
    ArenaVector<OverrideTarget> OverriddenTargets(...);
    ImplementationResolution ResolveInterfaceImplementation(...);
    OverloadSet GetMethodOverloadSet(...);
    void Clear();
};

The goal is shared semantic ownership, not a framework of separate public-looking service classes.

content.text:
Updated target design

MethodImplementationResolver

enum class ImplementationKind {
    NONE,
    CLASS_METHOD,
    SUPERCLASS_METHOD,
    INTERFACE_DEFAULT,
    INHERITED_SELECTED_DEFAULT,
    CONFLICT,
};

struct ImplementationTarget {
    ImplementationKind kind;
    Signature *signature;
    ir::AstNode *declaration;
    ETSObjectType *declaringType;
};

class MethodImplementationResolver {
public:
    ImplementationResolution ResolveImplementation(ETSObjectType *classType,
                                                   MethodKey key);
    bool HasCommonImplementation(ETSObjectType *classType,
                                 Signature *a,
                                 Signature *b); // convenience
};

Interface requirements need one group-based implementation resolution path, otherwise checker diagnostics and verifier/linker-visible emitted defaults can disagree.

Updated target design

Implementation resolution rules

  • Prefer concrete class/superclass methods when they override the interface requirement.
  • Collect applicable interface defaults only when no class implementation exists.
  • Remove defaults overridden by more specific subinterface defaults.
  • Preserve a superclass-selected default as inherited implementation when appropriate.
  • Use substituted generic interface views for parameterized defaults.
  • Return semantic selection/conflict only; emission strategy is planned by a separate lowering consumer.
// Usage: validation before ESE0187
auto r = impls.ResolveImplementation(classType, key);
if (r.IsSelected()) {
    return; // one implementation resolves the group
}
if (r.IsConflict()) {
    LogInterfaceDefaultConflict(classType, key, r.ConflictingDefaults());
}

// Usage: verifier-safe emission

enum class OverloadSetKind {
    FUNCTION,
    INSTANCE_METHOD,
    STATIC_METHOD,
    INTERFACE_METHOD,
    CONSTRUCTOR,
    EXPLICIT_ALIAS,
};

struct OverloadSetKey {
    ETSObjectType *receiverType;  // null for free functions
    varbinder::Scope *scope;      // for functions / namespaces
    util::StringView name;
    OverloadSetKind kind;
};

class OverloadSetOracle {
public:
    const OverloadSet &GetOverloadSet(const OverloadSetKey &key);
    const OverloadSet &ExpandExplicitOverload(ir::OverloadDeclaration *decl);
    void Clear();
};
  • Builds sets lazily for calls, references, explicit overload validation, and constructor calls.
  • Preserves spec order: own methods, direct superclass, direct interfaces in source order.
  • Expands explicit overload entries that denote implicit overload groups.
  • Uses OverrideOracle to skip inherited candidates already represented by overriding methods.
  • Caches candidate lists only; call-specific generic inference stays outside the overload-set cache.
  • Caches results only until the next Recheck or plugin cache clear.
// Usage: method-call resolution
const auto &set = overloads.GetOverloadSet({receiverType, nullptr,
                                            name,
                                            OverloadSetKind::INSTANCE_METHOD});
auto selected = ResolveFirstApplicable(set, call->Arguments(), call->TypeParams());
call->SetSignature(selected.signature);
call->SetResolvedCallTarget(selected.ToCallTarget());
Generics-specific design

Inherited generic signatures are viewpoint-dependent

Generics are not a corner case for this feature. Override and overload answers for inherited generic methods depend on how a generic supertype is instantiated by the current derived type.

struct SupertypeView {
    ETSObjectType *rootType;
    ETSObjectType *declaringType;
    ETSObjectType *instantiatedType;
    SubstitutionMap substitution;
};

class GenericViewResolver {
public:
    SupertypeView ViewOfSupertype(ETSObjectType *rootType,
                                  ETSObjectType *declaringType);
    Signature *ViewSignatureFrom(const SupertypeView &view,
                                 Signature *originalSignature);
};
  • OverrideOracle compares derived methods against inherited view signatures, not always original declaration signatures.
  • OverloadSetOracle adds inherited generic candidates using the correct receiver-type view.
  • MethodImplementationResolver resolves parameterized interface defaults using the correct substituted view.
  • Bridge generation uses the same view signature to decide whether a runtime adapter is needed.
  • Substituted signature views should be cached until Recheck or plugin cache clear.
  • Generic type-parameter constraint variance needs a consistent rule; clarify spec wording if needed.

                     baseDeclaringType, derivedType, baseDecl};
auto decision = overrides.CheckOverride(baseView, derivedView);

edits.oldText:
The relation services should have an acyclic dependency order:

```text
GenericViewResolver
    -> OverrideOracle
        -> MethodImplementationResolver
        -> bridge/default emission planners

GenericViewResolver
    -> OverloadSetOracle
        -> call resolution
```

Rules:

- `GenericViewResolver` is the lowest-level helper for substituted views.
- `OverrideOracle` may consume `GenericViewResolver`.
- `OverloadSetOracle` may consume `GenericViewResolver` and `OverrideOracle` for inherited candidate suppression.
- `MethodImplementationResolver` may consume `GenericViewResolver` and `OverrideOracle` for default dominance.
- `OverrideOracle` must not depend on `OverloadSetOracle` or `MethodImplementationResolver`; otherwise lazy caches can form cycles.
- Bridge/default emission planning consumes semantic decisions; it must not rediscover override/default semantics.
edits.newText:
The conceptual relation queries should have an acyclic dependency order, even if they are implemented as methods inside one `SemanticRelations` component:

```text
generic-view helpers
    -> override queries
        -> implementation resolution
        -> bridge/default emission consumers

generic-view helpers
    -> method overload-set queries
        -> call resolution
```

Rules:

- generic-view helpers are the lowest-level helpers for substituted views;

enum class MethodKind { METHOD, GETTER, SETTER };
enum class MemberDispatchKind { INSTANCE, STATIC };

struct MethodKey {
    util::StringView name;
    MethodKind kind;
    MemberDispatchKind dispatchKind;
    EffectiveParameterSignature parameters;
};

struct MethodView {
    Signature *originalSignature;
    Signature *viewSignature;
    ETSObjectType *declaringType;
    ETSObjectType *viewOwner;
    ir::AstNode *declaration;
    MethodKey key;
    bool isAbstract;
    bool isPrivate;
};

class OverrideOracle {
public:
    OverrideDecision CheckOverride(const MethodView &base,
                                   const MethodView &derived);

    ArenaVector<OverrideTarget> GetOverriddenTargets(ETSObjectType *owner,
                                                     const MethodView &derived);
};

- Parser And Program Construction (`parser`): detailed - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/parser.md`

- Variable Binding And Scopes (`varbinder`): detailed - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/varbinder.md`
- Semantic Checker And Types (`checker`): detailed - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/checker.md`
- Lowering Phases (`lowering`): detailed - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/lowering.md`
- Compiler Core And Bytecode Emission (`compiler_core`): detailed - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/compiler_core.md`
- AST Verifier (`ast_verifier`): skip - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/ast_verifier.md`
- Driver And Public API (`driver_public_api`): skip - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/driver_public_api.md`
- Tests Tooling And Documentation (`tests_tooling_docs`): detailed - `review/component_design/revisions/component-design-v1/components/tests_tooling_docs.md`

# Top-Level Architecture Revision 1

## Summary
Design `_override_` and `_overload_` around ETS overload sets, not TypeScript implementation-signature lists. Parser preserves syntax, binder/scopes form ordered overload-set facts, checker owns override validity and first-valid overload resolution, and lowering consumes checked metadata only.

## Goals
- Align overload/override behavior with the latest ArkTS technical-preview spec.
- Make overload-set formation deterministic for explicit lists, implicit overloads, inheritance, constructors, and imports.
- Move semantic decisions out of lowering while keeping codegen-facing metadata stable.
- Avoid repeated transitive-supertype and overload-candidate scans on hot checker paths.

## Non-Goals
- No immediate public API expansion unless runtime/reflection metadata requires it.
- No early synthetic AST rewriting as the semantic model.
- No TypeScript-style hidden implementation-signature model as the default ETS design.

## Architectural Overview (Approach)
The architecture introduces a checker-visible ETS semantic layer with four conceptual records: `ExplicitOverloadList`, `ImplicitOverloadEntity`, `OverloadSet`, and `ResolvedOverloadCall`. `ExplicitOverloadList` represents `overload name { ... }` declarations and their order; `ImplicitOverloadEntity` represents real callable declarations with the same name/scope; `OverloadSet` is the ordered candidate list formed by ETS rules; `ResolvedOverloadCall` stores the first valid selected entity and checked call metadata.

Spec ledger: ArkTS Spec 1.2.1-alpha TP5 anchors overload and override work in §§15.9, 15.9.1-15.9.3, 15.10, 15.10.1-15.10.4, 15.11, 15.11.1-15.11.10. The release feed confirms overload completion, first-match overload resolution, overload declaration grammar, constructor-name clarification, same-scope overload formation, static-type resolution, private overload clarification, no default values in overload signatures, no field-by-getter override, and overload declaration inheritance wording updates. Older public HTML confirms interface inheritance/override categories and interface property accessor equivalence in §§10.5-10.6.5.

## Benefits
- Correctness: overload resolution becomes “form spec-ordered set, pick first valid entity,” eliminating ad-hoc ranking.
- Performance: lookup becomes O(1) per owner/name/staticness/kind plus O(k) first-valid scan, with inherited indexes amortizing hierarchy traversal.
- Diagnostics: parser reports syntax, binder reports set formation/name accessibility, checker reports semantic override and call failures.
- Migration safety: existing overload lowerings can be kept behind a metadata adapter until semantic decisions are removed.

## Task Resolution Map
| Request Task | Architecture Resolution | Components | Interfaces / Flow | Risk | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Task 1 | Maintain a rule ledger from latest spec §§15.9-15.11 plus release deltas; divergences are blockers. | `spec-ledger` | Spec -> design constraints -> tests | latest PDF access | Ledger review against release feed |
| Task 2 | Inventory current behavior by phase: parser/IR syntax, binder refs/import flags, scopes-init linking/filtering, checker validation/resolution, lowering helpers/mapping, public overload info. | `current-behavior-inventory` | Repo scan -> behavior map | hidden lowering semantics | Focused code review |
| Task 3 | Use `ExplicitOverloadList`, `ImplicitOverloadEntity`, `OverloadSet`, `ResolvedOverloadCall`; no workaround flags. | `semantic-model` | Scope/type owns immutable ordered set | ABI metadata unknown | AST dump and metadata audit |
| Task 4 | Binder registers overload declarations and callable entities by same scope, owner, name, kind, staticness, constructor/accessor category. | `binder-and-scopes` | Parser IR -> group facts -> checker | imports/qualified names | Import/export overload tests |
| Task 5 | Checker validates override target existence, compatible signature, visibility, kind/staticness, generic substitution, accessor/field/property shape, interface obligations, inherited collisions. | `override-checker` | Inherited member index -> relation checks -> diagnostics | spec ambiguity on legacy cases | Negative `test/ast` matrix |
| Task 6 | Resolver forms ETS overload sets, preserves explicit-list order, inserts implicit/super/interface/constructor candidates per spec, skips duplicates, selects first valid. | `call-resolution` | Lookup -> ordered set -> first valid -> metadata | lambda/generic contextual typing | Runtime first-match tests |
| Task 7 | Lowering consumes group id, selected callable, helper need, async/interface/bridge facts; it does not choose overloads or override targets. | `lowering-contract` | Checker metadata -> lowering adapter -> codegen | current AST mutation dependency | Lowering semantic-branch audit |
| Task 8 | Add per owner/name indexes, inherited-set cache, signature-key cache, relation-result cache, and diagnostic rendering caps. | `performance-model` | Immutable arena records, checker-lifetime caches | memory growth | Compile-time/RSS counters |
| Task 9 | Diagnostics map to spec triggers only; unspecified behavior is marked spec ambiguity. | `diagnostics` | Failure reason -> diagnostic category -> test | legacy test drift | Diagnostic golden tests |
| Task 10 | Migrate in phases: spec/inventory, semantic model, binder grouping, override checker, call resolver, lowering adapter, public metadata decision, tests/perf gates. | `migration-plan` | Phase gates with rollback at metadata boundary | cross-phase churn | Patch-level review gates |
| Task 11 | Tests cover negative diagnostics in `test/ast`, runnable dispatch in `test/runtime/ets`, plus scale cases. | `test-matrix` | Rule -> test category -> suite | brittle legacy tests | Targeted test run |
| Task 12 | Validate smoke, runner, compile benchmarks, cache counters, RSS, and no major frontend regression. | `validation-metrics` | Build dir commands -> metrics report | noisy benchmarks | Repeat 3-run median |

## Affected Components
- [id: a1] `parser/ETSparser*` — parse overload declarations, overload-list elements, modifier legality, constructors, accessors, and override/static syntax only. Source: spec §§15.10-15.11, release feed.
- [id: a2] `ir/base/overloadDeclaration*`, `ir/base/methodDefinition*` — preserve syntax/source order and existing codegen-facing metadata; semantic identity lives in side records. Source: ref:typescript, ref:kotlin.
- [id: a3] `varbinder/ETSBinder*` and scopes init — bind overload names, imports/exports, same-scope membership, and owner/name/staticness/kind grouping. Source: spec §15.11.1, release feed.
- [id: a4] `checker/ETSchecker*`, `checker/ets/object.cpp`, `function.cpp`, `helpers.cpp` — own override validation, overload-set formation, first-valid call resolution, and diagnostics. Source: spec §§15.9-15.11.
- [id: a5] ETS type relation/signature logic — provide override-compatible, overload-equivalent, assignability, generic substitution, optional/rest arity, and erasure-aware checks. Source: spec §§15.9.3, 15.10.4.
- [id: a6] overload lowerings and bridge/interface lowerings — consume checked facts for helper generation, call mapping, async overloads, interface properties, and bridge behavior. Source: ref:kotlin.
- [id: a7] `public` overload metadata — retain only if required for plugin/runtime/reflection compatibility. Source: assumption.
- [id: a8] `test/ast`, `test/runtime/ets` — encode diagnostics, runnable selection, inheritance, interfaces, constructors, imports, generics, accessors, and scale behavior. Source: AGENTS test policy.

## Competitor Analysis
- [id: c1] `Kotlin FIR` - Kotlin’s reusable override checker, use-site member scopes, and candidate metadata support cached inherited lookups. ETS should adapt the cache/metadata split, but not Kotlin’s most-specific ranking where ETS requires first-valid selection.
- [id: c2] `TypeScript` - TypeScript’s signature arrays and failure buckets are useful for diagnostics and caching. ETS must reject TS’s hidden implementation-signature assumption for explicit overload declarations and use ETS overload-set formation instead.

## Risks and Mitigations
- Latest spec ambiguity or inaccessible text — mitigation: keep a divergence ledger and block behavior not anchored to §§15.9-15.11 — severity: high.
- Lowering currently depends on AST overload links — mitigation: transition through a checked-metadata adapter — severity: high.
- Public overload metadata is ABI-visible — mitigation: audit before removing or reshaping metadata — severity: medium.
- Cache memory growth — mitigation: checker-lifetime arena allocation, absent-name fast paths, capped diagnostic candidate rendering — severity: medium.
- Legacy tests encode obsolete behavior — mitigation: classify as spec divergence, not rationale — severity: medium.

# Component Design: Semantic Checker And Types
Component ID: checker
Decision: detailed

## Summary
The checker must become the semantic owner of ETS `_override_` validation, overload-set finalization, first-valid overload resolution, and checked metadata exported to lowering. The design adds checker-local typed signature records, inherited-member indexes, structured diagnostics, and call/override metadata without moving syntax or structural lowering decisions into checker.

## Top-Level Alignment
This component implements the approved architecture where binder supplies grouped overload facts, checker validates and resolves them, and lowering consumes checked facts only. The checker participates through `ETSChecker`, ETS object/function type logic, `TypeRelation`, signature compatibility helpers, inherited member lookup, diagnostics, and resolved-call metadata.

## Tasks

### Task 1: Checker Rule Matrix Define
Request Tasks: Task 1, Task 9
Description: The checker needs a compact rule matrix for every semantic overload and override decision it owns. This matrix anchors `ETSChecker`, `TypeRelation`, and diagnostic emission to ArkTS spec sections rather than legacy test behavior. It also marks cases that checker must defer as spec ambiguity instead of inventing new compile-time errors.
Dependancies: none
Detailed Design: Add a checker-owned rule matrix covering override target existence, signature compatibility, visibility, kind/staticness, generics, accessors, interface obligations, inherited collisions, overload applicability, first-valid selection, and no-valid-call failures. Change checker diagnostics to reference rule categories from this matrix when reporting overload/override failures. Remove ad-hoc checker-only semantic branches that cannot be mapped to a listed rule category. `ETSChecker` uses the matrix as the local source for semantic failure classification, while parser and binder continue to own syntax and grouping diagnostics.
Acceptance Criteria: Every checker diagnostic category for overload/override maps to a matrix entry with a spec section or ambiguity marker. No checker semantic error for these features is emitted without a matrix category. The matrix distinguishes parser, binder, checker, and lowering ownership for each rule.
Workload: 0.6 MM

### Task 2: Checker Behavior Inventory Map
Request Tasks: Task 2, Task 10
Description: Existing checker behavior must be inventoried before semantic ownership changes because overload and override logic may be split across object, function, helper, and call-checking paths. The inventory is checker-local and identifies which decisions already belong to `ETSChecker`, which are duplicated in type relation helpers, and which are only consumed from lowering metadata. It provides the migration boundary for replacing behavior without changing parser or lowering responsibilities.
Dependancies: Checker Rule Matrix Define
Detailed Design: Add a component-local behavior map for current override validation, overload call resolution, signature compatibility, inherited lookup, accessor/property checks, constructor handling, and diagnostic emission. Change the migration notes for checker tasks to classify each path as keep, replace, or redirect to checked metadata. Remove no functionality in this task; it produces the precise checker deltas used by later tasks. `ETSChecker`, ETS object type checking, function checking, helper utilities, and type relation APIs are the named inventory anchors.
Acceptance Criteria: The map identifies every checker-local overload/override decision point and its target owner after migration. It explicitly lists semantic branches that must stop being duplicated by lowering. Later checker tasks can cite the inventory entry they replace.
Workload: 0.5 MM

### Task 3: Typed Signature Facts Add
Request Tasks: Task 3, Task 5, Task 6, Task 8
Description: The checker needs canonical typed signature facts so override checks and overload resolution do not repeatedly walk AST nodes. These facts belong in checker/type logic because they include normalized parameter types, arity, rest/optional shape, type parameter arity, visibility, staticness, member kind, accessor category, and implementation identity. They are side records over existing declarations, not new AST flags.
Dependancies: Checker Behavior Inventory Map
Detailed Design: Add arena-allocated typed signature records for callable, constructor, accessor, and property-like members, with compact ids usable by checker caches and lowering metadata. Change checker signature comparison and call applicability paths to consume these records instead of reconstructing declaration facts from AST nodes on each check. Remove local workaround flags or pointer-identity comparisons where a signature key or `TypeRelation` query can express the same fact. `ETSChecker` builds the records after binder-provided group facts are available, and `TypeRelation` consumes normalized type slots for compatibility checks.
Acceptance Criteria: Override validation and overload resolution can run from typed signature ids without directly re-reading parameter lists for common checks. Signature records distinguish static/instance, method/accessor/constructor, visibility, optional/rest arity, and generic arity. Records are immutable after construction and allocated with checker lifetime.
Workload: 1.8 MM

### Task 4: InheritedMemberIndex Cache Add
Request Tasks: Task 5, Task 8
Description: Override checks and inherited overload candidates need a checker-owned cache to avoid repeated transitive supertype scans. `InheritedMemberIndex` owns inherited group slices keyed by owner type, name, staticness, member kind, and accessor/constructor category. It does not own same-scope overload declarations and does not duplicate the final call view.
Dependancies: Typed Signature Facts Add
Detailed Design: Add lazy inherited-member indexes for ETS object/interface types, populated from finalized supertype member groups and typed signature ids. Change override validation and overload candidate collection to ask the index for inherited slices instead of walking direct and transitive bases repeatedly. Remove repeated local supertype scans from hot checker paths once the index is available. The index stores immutable inherited candidate slices and exposes ordered iterators; `OverloadSetView` layers those iterators with same-scope candidates when a specific validation or call resolution asks for them.
Acceptance Criteria: Repeated override checks for the same owner/name/staticness/kind reuse one inherited index entry. Diamond inheritance uses visited type ids and deterministic ordering. `InheritedMemberIndex` is the only checker entity that materializes inherited candidate slices; `OverloadSetView` only references those slices.
Workload: 2.0 MM

### Task 5: OverloadSetView Finalize
Request Tasks: Task 3, Task 4, Task 6, Task 8
Description: The checker needs a non-owning overload-set view that combines binder-provided same-scope groups with inherited index slices in spec order. This view is the local boundary between binder grouping and checker resolution. It contains declared/same-scope typed candidates plus references to inherited slices, then produces an ordered iterator for validation or call resolution without duplicating inherited storage.
Dependancies: InheritedMemberIndex Cache Add
Detailed Design: Add `OverloadSetView` as a checker-local view over explicit overload-list signatures, implicit same-scope callable entities, constructor candidates, and inherited slices from `InheritedMemberIndex`. Change call and override paths to form a view from owner/name/staticness/kind lookup before checking candidates. Remove transient ad-hoc vectors that merge candidates differently in separate checker paths. `ETSChecker` controls view creation, typed signature records provide candidate facts, and `InheritedMemberIndex` supplies inherited slices by reference.
Acceptance Criteria: Explicit overload-list order, implicit same-scope order, constructor order, and inherited order are visible through one deterministic iterator. The view does not own inherited candidate storage and cannot mutate typed signatures. Checker users can request the same ordered view for ordinary member calls, `super` calls, constructor calls, and override validation.
Workload: 1.4 MM

### Task 6: OverrideValidator Implement
Request Tasks: Task 5, Task 9, Task 11
Description: Override validation belongs in checker because it requires typed signatures, inherited member facts, visibility, generic substitution, and type-relation queries. The validator checks declared `_override_` members against inherited overload views and reports spec-category diagnostics. It also validates inherited collisions that arise even when no explicit override marker is present.
Dependancies: OverloadSetView Finalize
Detailed Design: Add an `OverrideValidator` service used by `ETSChecker` for methods, accessors, properties, interface members, and static/instance-separated member families. Change existing override checks to call the validator with typed signature ids and inherited `OverloadSetView` iterators. Remove duplicated override-target searches and hard-coded AST/type pattern checks that are replaced by `TypeRelation` compatibility predicates. The validator returns structured results for valid override, missing target, illegal kind/staticness mismatch, visibility violation, generic incompatibility, accessor/property mismatch, and inherited collision.
Acceptance Criteria: Checker reports distinct diagnostics for missing override target, illegal override, accidental conflict, and inherited-member collision. Validation uses `TypeRelation` for signature/type compatibility and does not compare type names or type pointers for semantic equality. Accessor/property and interface obligations are checked through typed signature categories.
Workload: 3.0 MM

### Task 7: FirstValidResolver Implement
Request Tasks: Task 6, Task 8, Task 9, Task 11
Description: Overload call resolution must be checker-owned and must select the first valid candidate from the spec-ordered overload set. The resolver uses cheap filters first, then type argument handling, generic substitution, lambda/context-sensitive compatibility, and `TypeRelation` checks. It records structured failure buckets when no candidate is valid.
Dependancies: OverloadSetView Finalize
Detailed Design: Add `FirstValidOverloadResolver` that consumes `OverloadSetView`, call arguments, optional type arguments, receiver/static context, and call kind. Change member-call, `super` call, constructor-call, and ordinary callable resolution paths to use the resolver and attach a `ResolvedOverloadCall` record. Remove ad-hoc ranking or best-candidate branches that conflict with first-valid selection. The resolver scans the ordered view once on the successful path, skips inaccessible or wrong-staticness candidates, applies arity and type-argument prefilters, checks compatibility, and returns the first candidate that passes.
Acceptance Criteria: Tests or checker-level traces verify deterministic first-valid choice for explicit overload lists, implicit same-scope entities, inherited candidates, constructors, `super` calls, and ordinary member calls. When no candidate is valid, the resolver preserves failure buckets for arity, type argument, accessibility, and type compatibility diagnostics. Successful resolution stores selected group id, signature id, implementation id, inferred type arguments, and argument mapping.
Workload: 3.5 MM

### Task 8: Checker Metadata Export Shape
Request Tasks: Task 7, Task 10
Description: Lowering needs checked semantic facts, but checker must not decide structural helper generation policy. The export shape should contain validated mappings and selected implementation ids only. Lowering remains responsible for choosing helper emission, bridge structure, async wrappers, and codegen-specific transformations from those facts.
Dependancies: OverrideValidator Implement, FirstValidResolver Implement
Detailed Design: Add checker-exported records for `ResolvedOverloadCall`, validated override target mapping, interface obligation mapping, accessor/property mapping, and selected implementation identity. Change checker-to-lowering handoff to expose these records through existing metadata channels or a minimal side table. Remove semantic lowerability decisions from checker export names and keep helper-policy fields out unless they represent a validated prerequisite fact. `ETSChecker` owns record creation; lowering consumes the records and decides structural generation.
Acceptance Criteria: Lowering can identify the selected implementation for every checked overloaded call without re-running overload resolution. Override/interface/accessor mappings exported by checker identify validated semantic targets, not helper plans. No exported checker record requires lowering to inspect rejected overload candidates for semantic decisions.
Workload: 1.6 MM

### Task 9: Relation And Diagnostic Caches Add
Request Tasks: Task 8, Task 9, Task 12
Description: The checker hot path needs caches for repeated signature relation and diagnostic rendering work. These caches belong beside `TypeRelation`, typed signature records, and call resolution because they reuse checker-lifetime semantic facts. They must improve repeated overload and override checks without creating global mutable state.
Dependancies: Typed Signature Facts Add, FirstValidResolver Implement
Detailed Design: Add checker-lifetime caches for signature equivalence, override compatibility, assignability/applicability relation results, required/rest arity facts, and capped diagnostic candidate rendering. Change resolver and validator loops to consult caches before expensive `TypeRelation` calls. Remove repeated construction of equivalent diagnostic candidate lists on the successful path. Cache keys use typed signature ids, normalized type ids, relation kind, and substitution context where required.
Acceptance Criteria: Repeated calls over the same overload group reuse relation cache entries. Diagnostics render a bounded number of rejected candidates while preserving full internal failure classification. Cache lifetime is tied to checker/program lifetime and no cache entry depends on mutable AST shape.
Workload: 1.8 MM

### Task 10: Checker Test Matrix Define
Request Tasks: Task 5, Task 6, Task 9, Task 11, Task 12
Description: Checker behavior changes require targeted semantic coverage for diagnostics and selected overload metadata. The matrix is component-local because it maps checker entities and diagnostic categories to compile-fail and runnable cases. It also defines scale probes for overload and inheritance hot paths.
Dependancies: OverrideValidator Implement, FirstValidResolver Implement, Relation And Diagnostic Caches Add
Detailed Design: Add a checker-focused test matrix covering override targets, inherited overload sets, interfaces, accessors, constructors, static/instance separation, visibility, generics, optional/rest parameters, first-valid selection, no-valid-call diagnostics, and scale cases. Change existing overload/override tests to reference the new checker diagnostic categories where behavior is spec-aligned. Remove reliance on legacy lowering behavior as the explanation for semantic outcomes. The matrix assigns negative diagnostics to compile-time tests, runnable selected-call behavior to runtime tests, and performance probes to validation counters.
Acceptance Criteria: Every checker diagnostic category has at least one mapped negative case. First-valid behavior is covered for explicit, implicit, inherited, constructor, `super`, and member-call sources. Scale cases exercise large overload sets, deep inheritance, diamond interfaces, and repeated generic/lambda calls.
Workload: 0.8 MM

## Cross-Cutting Constraints
- Checker semantics must be spec-ledger driven — the approved architecture treats unspecified behavior as ambiguity rather than implementation freedom (source: spec §§15.9-15.11)
- Typed signature and overload records are checker-lifetime immutable — this preserves the architecture’s side-record model and avoids AST mutation in checker (source: ref:kotlin-fir-descriptor-override-overload)
- First-valid selection is the resolver rule — every candidate source must feed the same ordered view before compatibility checks (source: ref:microsoft/TypeScript)
- Lowering policy stays outside checker — checker exports validated semantic facts and selected ids only (source: external:index.md)
- Caches must be local to checker/type relation lifetime — performance work must not introduce global state or stale AST-dependent entries (source: ref:kotlin-fir-descriptor-override-overload)

## Data And Control Flow
- Binder group facts enter checker — `ETSChecker` builds typed signature records — checker owns semantic identity after binding (source: spec §15.11.1)
- Typed signatures feed inherited indexing — `InheritedMemberIndex` materializes inherited slices once — overload views reference those slices without owning them (source: ref:kotlin-fir-descriptor-override-overload)
- Overload views feed validation and calls — `OverrideValidator` and `FirstValidOverloadResolver` consume the same ordered candidate interface — ordering is centralized (source: ref:microsoft/TypeScript)
- Resolver output feeds metadata export — `ResolvedOverloadCall` stores selected signature, implementation, inferred types, and argument mapping — lowering consumes ids only (source: external:index.md)
- Diagnostics use failure buckets — resolver and validator return structured reasons — rendering is capped and checker-owned (source: ref:microsoft/TypeScript)

## Component Interactions
- [id: i1] `varbinder grouped overload facts` -> `ETSChecker typed signatures` — binder provides same-scope group identity and declaration order; checker creates typed semantic records (source: spec §15.11.1)
- [id: i2] `ETS object/function type logic` -> `TypeRelation` — override and overload compatibility use relation APIs instead of hard-coded type tests (source: spec §§15.9.3, 15.10.4)
- [id: i3] `InheritedMemberIndex` -> `OverloadSetView` — inherited candidates are stored in index slices and layered into views by reference (source: ref:kotlin-fir-descriptor-override-overload)
- [id: i4] `FirstValidOverloadResolver` -> `checker metadata export` — selected overload facts become `ResolvedOverloadCall` records for lowering (source: ref:microsoft/TypeScript)
- [id: i5] `OverrideValidator` -> `lowering consumers` — validated override/interface/accessor mappings are exported as semantic targets, not helper-generation decisions (source: external:index.md)

## Rationale
The checker is materially affected because the approved architecture moves override validity, overload-set formation for semantic use, first-valid call resolution, diagnostics, and performance caches into checker/type logic. Existing parser, binder, and lowering components remain separate owners of syntax, grouping input, and structural transformation, while checker becomes the single semantic source of truth.

# Component Design: Lowering Phases
Component ID: lowering
Decision: detailed

## Summary
Lowering phases are materially affected because overload and override decisions move to binder/checker metadata. Lowering keeps structural work only: helper generation, call mapping, async/interface transformations, and bridge emission from checked facts.

## Top-Level Alignment
This component implements Task 7 of the top-level architecture by making lowering a consumer of `OverloadSet`, `ResolvedOverloadCall`, and override mapping metadata. It preserves codegen-facing behavior while removing semantic overload choice and override-target discovery from lowering phases.

## Tasks

### Task 1: DeclareOverload consumes group facts
Request Tasks: Task 7, Task 10
Description: `declareOverloadLowering` currently participates in shaping overload declarations for later compilation. Its local role becomes translating checked overload-group facts into the structural helper form expected by downstream lowering and codegen.
Dependancies: none
Detailed Design: Add a lowering-local adapter view for checked overload group facts: group id, declared signature ids, implementation callable id, helper emission policy, source order, and constructor/accessor category. Change `declareOverloadLowering` to read this adapter instead of rediscovering overload declarations from AST neighborhoods or choosing an implementation method itself. Remove local semantic checks that decide whether overload declarations are valid or whether an implementation is compatible; those states arrive as already-checked metadata. The phase hands generated helper structure and preserved codegen-facing metadata to subsequent lowering phases.
Acceptance Criteria: `declareOverloadLowering` has one metadata entrypoint for overload group facts, produces the same helper/codegen-facing structure for checked valid groups, and contains no branch that selects a valid overload candidate or reports user-facing overload validity diagnostics.
Workload: 2.0 MM

### Task 2: OverloadMapping uses resolved calls
Request Tasks: Task 6, Task 7
Description: `overloadMappingLowering` is the lowering-side consumer for call-site overload decisions. Its local role is to rewrite or annotate calls using `ResolvedOverloadCall`, not to scan candidates or infer which overload wins.
Dependancies: DeclareOverload consumes group facts
Detailed Design: Add a lowering-local resolved-call access path carrying selected callable id, selected signature id, implementation target id, inferred type arguments where already materialized, and argument mapping/default/rest facts. Change `overloadMappingLowering` to transform call nodes from that resolved metadata and remove candidate collection, compatibility filtering, first-valid selection, and ambiguity fallback logic from the phase. The phase interacts with call-expression lowering and method-call lowering only through selected target metadata. Missing resolved metadata is treated as an internal consistency failure for invalid phase ordering, not as a semantic diagnostic.
Acceptance Criteria: Every overloaded call lowered by `overloadMappingLowering` is driven by a selected resolved-call record, and the phase no longer performs overload candidate scans, type-relation checks, or best-candidate selection.
Workload: 2.5 MM

### Task 3: Async overload lowering reads policy
Request Tasks: Task 7
Description: Async overload handling may need wrapper/helper generation after overload validity is known. Its local role is to apply a checked helper policy for async overload groups without deciding declaration compatibility.
Dependancies: DeclareOverload consumes group facts, OverloadMapping uses resolved calls
Detailed Design: Add async-specific fields to the lowering adapter: async helper requirement, implementation target, emitted wrapper identity, and source signature association. Change async overload lowering to consume these fields when generating wrappers or mappings. Remove local checks that decide whether async overload declarations are compatible with the implementation signature. The async lowering path passes wrapper identities forward to call mapping and bridge emission through the same checked group id.
Acceptance Criteria: Async overload wrappers are emitted only from checked async helper policy, preserve selected implementation identity, and do not perform overload validity or implementation-compatibility checks in lowering.
Workload: 1.5 MM

### Task 4: Interface property lowering uses mappings
Request Tasks: Task 5, Task 7
Description: Interface property and accessor lowering must agree with checker-owned override/interface obligations. Its local role is to emit the structural accessor/property representation from validated override mappings.
Dependancies: DeclareOverload consumes group facts
Detailed Design: Add a lowering view for checked interface/accessor mappings: source accessor id, target interface member id, getter/setter role, property-pair identity, bridge need, and override group id where relevant. Change interface property lowering to consume these mappings and remove local target discovery between fields, getters, setters, and interface properties. The phase emits existing structural nodes or helper methods from the mapping and hands bridge facts to bridge/interface lowering. It does not decide whether a field can override a getter or whether an accessor pair satisfies an interface member.
Acceptance Criteria: Interface property lowering emits accessor/property structures from checked mappings, and no lowering branch performs accessor-vs-field override validation or interface obligation discovery.
Workload: 2.0 MM

### Task 5: Bridge lowering consumes override facts
Request Tasks: Task 5, Task 7
Description: Bridge and interface-related lowerings may need override information to preserve dispatch behavior. Their local role is to emit bridge structures from checker-approved override targets and signature substitutions.
Dependancies: Interface property lowering uses mappings
Detailed Design: Add a bridge input record containing overriding callable id, overridden target id, substituted signature id, staticness/kind category, visibility already accepted by checker, and bridge emission requirement. Change bridge lowering to emit bridges from this record and remove inherited-member scans or override-target searches from lowering. The bridge path coordinates with method lowering and interface lowering through stable callable ids rather than AST pattern checks. Existing bridge output shape is preserved unless checked metadata explicitly says no bridge is required.
Acceptance Criteria: Bridge lowering emits bridges only from checked override facts and contains no inherited hierarchy traversal, override compatibility check, or override target selection.
Workload: 2.0 MM

### Task 6: Lowering asserts metadata coverage
Request Tasks: Task 2, Task 7, Task 12
Description: Lowering needs a component-local coverage check to ensure all overload/override-sensitive paths are driven by checked metadata. Its local role is to make semantic ownership violations visible during development and validation.
Dependancies: DeclareOverload consumes group facts, OverloadMapping uses resolved calls, Async overload lowering reads policy, Interface property lowering uses mappings, Bridge lowering consumes override facts
Detailed Design: Add lowering-phase assertions or verifier hooks that check required metadata exists before overload declaration lowering, overloaded call mapping, async helper emission, interface property lowering, and bridge emission. Change lowering phase diagnostics so user-facing semantic errors are not produced here; failures identify missing metadata or invalid phase ordering. Remove fallback code paths that silently recompute overload or override facts when metadata is absent. The checks report the component-local lowering entity and the missing group/call/override record.
Acceptance Criteria: A lowering metadata audit can prove every overload/override-sensitive lowering path has a checked record, and invalid metadata absence fails through internal consistency reporting rather than semantic recomputation.
Workload: 1.0 MM

## Cross-Cutting Constraints
- Lowering consumes checked facts only — semantic overload resolution and override validity belong to checker-owned records before lowering runs (source: spec §15.9-15.11)
- Preserve codegen-facing metadata shape during migration — existing runtime/helper behavior must stay stable while semantic ownership moves out of lowering (source: ref:kotlin)
- Use stable ids, not AST neighborhood inference — group, signature, callable, and override identities must be explicit across lowering phases (source: ref:typescript)
- Keep structural transformations in lowering — helper, wrapper, bridge, and interface-property emission remain lowering responsibilities (source: assumption §7)

## Data And Control Flow
- Checked overload group facts arrive before `declareOverloadLowering` — checker metadata to declaration lowering — lowering emits helper structure without semantic validation (source: spec §15.10)
- Resolved call metadata arrives before `overloadMappingLowering` — call resolver to call mapping lowering — lowering rewrites calls to selected implementation targets (source: spec §15.11)
- Checked override/accessor mappings arrive before interface and bridge lowering — override checker to structural lowerings — lowering emits accessors and bridges from approved mappings (source: spec §15.9)
- Lowering metadata coverage checks run inside overload-sensitive phases — lowering adapters and assertions — absence of metadata is internal phase-order failure (source: assumption §12)

## Component Interactions
- [id: i1] `checker resolved-call metadata` -> `overloadMappingLowering` — selected signature, implementation target, argument mapping, and inferred type arguments are consumed without candidate scanning (source: ref:typescript)
- [id: i2] `checker overload-group metadata` -> `declareOverloadLowering` — group id, implementation callable, declaration order, and helper policy drive helper generation (source: ref:kotlin)
- [id: i3] `checker override/accessor metadata` -> `interface property lowering` — validated getter/setter/property mappings drive structural interface-property emission (source: spec §15.9)
- [id: i4] `checker override metadata` -> `bridge lowering` — validated target and substituted signature facts drive bridge emission (source: ref:kotlin)

## Rationale
Lowering is affected because the approved architecture explicitly removes overload selection and override-target validation from lowering while keeping helper, mapping, async, interface, and bridge transformations there. The component work is therefore to replace lowering-local semantic discovery with checked metadata adapters and coverage checks.

# Component Design: Parser And Program Construction
Component ID: parser
Decision: detailed

## Summary
The parser is affected, but the work is refactoring and fact preservation rather than adding overload or override parsing from scratch. `ETSParser` already recognizes overload declarations and override modifiers; this design makes the parser syntax-only, current-state aware, and explicit about the facts binder/checker need.

## Top-Level Alignment
The approved architecture keeps parser ownership limited to concrete syntax, source order, modifier tokens, named or qualified overload-list entries, constructor/accessor syntax, and AST construction. Overload-set formation, override validity, duplicate signature checks, and call resolution are owned by binder/checker.

## Tasks

### Task 1: ETSParser rule inventory
Request Tasks: Task 1, Task 2, Task 9
Description: Inventory the existing `ETSParser` overload declaration and `_override_` modifier paths against the spec ledger for parser-owned syntax only. The output is a parser-local rule table that separates grammar acceptance, modifier placement, token ranges, and recoverable syntax diagnostics from binder/checker semantics.
Dependancies: none
Detailed Design: Add a parser-local rule inventory for overload declaration forms, named entries, qualified entries, constructor entries, accessors, static/override modifier positions, optional/rest parameter syntax, and source-order preservation. Change existing parser documentation or comments around these paths to mark semantic checks as downstream-owned. Remove parser-side assumptions that classify valid syntax as invalid because of overload-set membership, override target existence, duplicate/equivalent signatures, or accessibility.
Acceptance Criteria: The inventory names the existing `ETSParser` entrypoints and AST construction facts for overload and override syntax. Each parser diagnostic category is syntax-only, and semantic categories are explicitly assigned to binder/checker without changing parse acceptance.
Workload: 0.5 MM

### Task 2: OverloadDecl entries preserve keys
Request Tasks: Task 3, Task 4
Description: Normalize parser construction of overload declaration facts so binder receives stable overload-list entries. The parser must preserve ETS named and qualified overload-list entries, source order, containing-scope order, constructor category, accessor category, and modifier tokens without creating a TypeScript-style hidden implementation-signature model.
Dependancies: ETSParser rule inventory
Detailed Design: Add an explicit parser handoff shape in the constructed overload declaration node: declared key, ordered entry list, qualification shape, constructor/accessor/method category, static modifier presence, source ordinal, and source ranges. Change overload declaration construction so named and qualified entries are represented directly instead of being inferred later from source neighborhood. Remove any parser dependency on adjacent implementation methods as the source of overload identity; ordinary callable declarations remain ordinary AST nodes and become `ImplicitOverloadEntity` inputs only after binding.
Acceptance Criteria: AST dumps or parser tests show overload declarations retaining ordered named entries, qualified entries, constructor entries, and modifier ranges. Binder can consume the constructed overload declaration facts without scanning nearby methods to recover the overload-list key.
Workload: 1.0 MM

### Task 3: Callable categories mark syntax
Request Tasks: Task 3, Task 4, Task 6
Description: Ensure parser-created method, constructor, and accessor nodes expose only syntactic category facts needed for later overload grouping. This keeps `ETSParser` responsible for concrete callable shape while checker owns signature compatibility and overload resolution.
Dependancies: OverloadDecl entries preserve keys
Detailed Design: Add or normalize parser-populated callable category facts for method, constructor, getter, setter, static instance, async where syntactically present, type parameters, optional parameters, rest parameters, and return-type annotation presence. Change AST construction so these facts are available uniformly for overload declarations and real callable declarations. Remove parser logic that interprets those facts as overload equivalence, implementation compatibility, first-match priority, or override compatibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Parser output distinguishes method, constructor, getter, and setter syntax for both overload declaration entries and real callable declarations. Semantically invalid but syntactically valid combinations parse successfully and remain available for downstream diagnostics.
Workload: 0.8 MM

### Task 4: Override modifier stays syntactic
Request Tasks: Task 5, Task 9
Description: Keep `_override_` parsing as modifier capture on declarations while preventing parser ownership of override validity. Parser diagnostics remain limited to malformed modifier placement or duplicate tokens according to grammar.
Dependancies: ETSParser rule inventory
Detailed Design: Add or normalize source-range preservation for `_override_` on method, accessor, and other declaration forms allowed by the grammar. Change modifier parsing so `_override_` is passed through as syntax metadata to binder/checker with staticness and declaration category facts. Remove parser-side checks for inherited target existence, static/instance mismatch, visibility, accessor/field compatibility, generic compatibility, and interface obligations.
Acceptance Criteria: Declarations with `_override_` retain exact modifier metadata for checker diagnostics. Cases with no override target or incompatible inherited member still parse, while malformed token order or grammar-forbidden modifier placement remains a parser diagnostic.
Workload: 0.6 MM

### Task 5: Parser tests lock handoff facts
Request Tasks: Task 2, Task 9, Task 11
Description: Add focused parser and AST construction tests for the syntax facts this component owns. Tests should document current supported overload and override syntax while guarding against accidental semantic filtering in parser.
Dependancies: OverloadDecl entries preserve keys, Callable categories mark syntax, Override modifier stays syntactic
Detailed Design: Add parser tests for ordered overload declaration entries, qualified entry names, constructor overload declarations, accessor entries, static and override modifier capture, optional/rest parameter syntax, and recovery from malformed syntax. Change existing parser tests that expect semantic rejection to assert successful parse plus preserved syntax facts where the grammar allows it. Remove parser-test dependence on checker-owned duplicate, accessibility, override-target, or overload-resolution diagnostics.
Acceptance Criteria: Parser tests verify source order, qualification shape, callable category, constructor/accessor category, modifier ranges, and syntax diagnostics. No parser test requires duplicate overload-equivalence, missing override target, target accessibility, or call-resolution behavior.
Workload: 0.9 MM

## Cross-Cutting Constraints
- Parser remains syntax-only — overload sets and override validity are downstream semantic responsibilities (source: spec §15.9-15.11)
- Existing overload and override parser support is retained — the component work refines current parser facts rather than adding a new grammar family (source: assumption §current-state)
- Named and qualified overload-list entries are preserved — binder/checker need deterministic same-scope grouping inputs (source: spec §15.11.1)
- No TypeScript hidden implementation-signature model is introduced in parser — ETS semantic identity is formed from overload sets and real callable declarations (source: ref:typescript)

## Data And Control Flow
- Tokens are parsed by `ETSParser` — parser owns grammar acceptance, modifier ranges, declaration category, and source order before AST construction (source: assumption §parser)
- Overload declaration nodes are constructed — ordered named or qualified entries, constructor/accessor category, and source ordinal are retained as syntax facts (source: spec §15.10-15.11)
- Callable declaration nodes are constructed — real methods, constructors, getters, and setters remain independent AST declarations for binder grouping (source: assumption §semantic-model)
- Binder consumes parser facts — overload group formation uses parser-provided keys and ordinals without source-neighborhood inference (source: assumption §4)

## Component Interactions
- [id: i1] `ETSParser` -> `varbinder` — passes overload declaration key, ordered entry facts, qualification shape, modifier metadata, and containing-scope ordinal (source: spec §15.11.1)
- [id: i2] `ETSParser` -> `checker` — preserves `_override_`, callable category, constructor/accessor syntax, optional/rest parameters, and type-parameter syntax for semantic validation (source: spec §15.9-15.11)
- [id: i3] `parser tests` -> `parser contract` — verify syntax preservation and parser diagnostics without asserting semantic overload or override behavior (source: assumption §test-policy)

## Rationale
The parser is materially affected because the top-level architecture depends on deterministic syntax facts for later overload-set formation and override checking. Since overload declarations and override modifiers already exist, the concrete delta is to preserve ETS-specific named/qualified syntax and source-order handoff facts while removing or avoiding parser-side semantic coupling.
