content.text:
After interface validation uses shared override queries, add one default-method resolution path:

- collect applicable interface defaults for a class/method key;
- remove defaults overridden by more specific subinterface defaults;
- prefer concrete class/superclass implementations when present;
- preserve a superclass-selected default as the inherited implementation when no concrete class method exists;
- use substituted generic interface views;
- feed the selected method implementation into lowering/emission planning so verifier does not see unresolved multiple defaults.

This phase can be gradual at the API level, but checker diagnostics and default-method emission must agree before suppressed verifier/linker tests are re-enabled.

## Phase 10: bridge phases consume shared target discovery

Once shared override-query behavior is reliable:

- stop old semantic bridge rediscovery from disagreeing with shared relation queries;
- make bridge code query `OverriddenTargets` for each own concrete method;
- treat generic-substitution bridges and override-conversion bridges as reasons attached to the same override target, not as separate hierarchy searches;
- deduplicate by effective/assembly descriptor;
- preserve existing bridge body generation helpers where possible.

This should be one coherent switch to avoid duplicate or missing bridges. Physical bridge phases may stay split initially; what must become shared is semantic target discovery and descriptor deduplication.

## Phase 11: cleanup

After migration:

- reduce overload-specific property lookup flags;
- remove or shrink synthetic overload variable construction in `GetProperty`;
- remove duplicated override predicates;
- remove casual `CallSignatures().front()` in overload paths;
- make call resolution consume overload sets directly from shared relation queries.

---

## What can be done gradually

Safe gradual changes:

1. Add characterization tests.
2. Classify suppressed overriding failures by owning relation query group.
3. Add pure helper functions.
4. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision.
5. Audit `GetApparentType` and add effective-signature wrapper helpers.
6. Introduce one checker-owned `SemanticRelations`/`SemanticRelationCache` component with delegated query helpers.
7. Move method overload-set construction behind the shared relation component where currently needed.
8. Move override diagnostics and interface validation behind shared override queries.
9. Add method implementation resolution behind the same relation component.
10. Remove duplicate predicates after relation consumers are stable.

---

## What should be done all at once

Some changes must be atomic because partial migration would create inconsistent semantics.

| Change | Why it should be atomic |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit overload expansion | Validation, synthetic type construction, call resolution, and lowering must agree about candidate count/order. |
| Resolved call target representation | Checker and lowering must switch together from owner-variable assumptions to explicit target metadata. |
| Shared bridge target discovery switch | Running old semantic rediscovery and new relation-driven target discovery together risks duplicate or missing bridges. |
| Default-method emission switch | Checker implementation-resolution results and emitted/default-forwarding representation must agree, otherwise verifier/linker can still see multiple defaults. |
| Direct overload-set call resolution | `MemberExpression`, `CallExpression`, method references, explicit overloads, and lowering must agree. |
| Effective overload-equivalence across declaration kinds | Functions, methods, interfaces, and constructors must use the same language rule. |

---

## Recommended implementation order

1. Add characterization tests and classify suppressed overriding failures by relation query group.
2. Add pure override compatibility and overload-equivalence helpers.
3. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision checks.
4. Audit `GetApparentType`, add effective-signature wrappers, and use them for overload-equivalence.
5. Add checker-owned `SemanticRelations`/`SemanticRelationCache` with coarse cache clearing; conceptual `OverrideOracle`, `OverloadSetOracle`, method implementation, and generic-view query groups can be implemented as methods/helpers first.
6. Add generic view/substitution support for inherited signatures used by shared relation queries.
7. Implement explicit overload expansion as an atomic patch.
8. Move method overload-set construction into the shared relation component behind existing APIs where currently needed.
9. Migrate interface implementation/conflict checks to shared override and implementation-resolution queries.
10. Add verifier-safe selected-default emission based on implementation-resolution results.
11. Migrate overload-set duplicate suppression to shared override-target queries.
12. Make bridge phases consume shared override-target discovery/dedup; physical bridge-phase unification is optional initially.
13. Remove obsolete synthetic/ad-hoc overload paths.

---

## Workload estimation

Estimation model requested for planning:

```text
500 added C++ production lines ~= 1 man-month
```

Important assumptions:

- The estimate below is based on **added C++ production code**, not total churn. Refactoring may also delete or move code.
- Tests, diagnostics text, documentation, CI debugging, review iterations, and flaky investigation are listed separately where relevant because they are not well represented by added C++ lines.
- Ranges are intentionally broad because the current implementation is intertwined with checker, object type lookup, default-method resolution/emission, lowering, and bridge generation.
- The safest plan is still incremental: land small correctness-preserving steps instead of one large rewrite.

| Work item | Estimated added C++ LOC | Man-months by model | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Pure semantic helpers + overload-equivalence split + first effective-signature helpers | 600-900 | 1.2-1.8 | Introduces side-effect-free override compatibility, overload-equivalence, and effective signature type utilities. |
| `SemanticRelations` / `SemanticRelationCache` + base override-query caches | 600-900 | 1.2-1.8 | Includes query API, cache clearing, inherited method candidate cache, override pair cache, and common-implementation query. |
| Method overload-set queries + spec ordering + explicit overload expansion | 900-1400 | 1.8-2.8 | Largest early chunk. Expands implicit overload groups in explicit overload lists and centralizes method overload-set order where needed. |
| Generic view/substitution support for relation services | 500-900 | 1.0-1.8 | Adds substituted inherited signature views, generic candidate/default handling, and bridge/override support for generic supertypes. |
| Resolved call target metadata + lowering consumption | 350-650 | 0.7-1.3 | Adds selected target metadata and updates explicit-overload lowering to consume it instead of rediscovering owners. |
| Migrate class/interface validation to shared override queries | 700-1100 | 1.4-2.2 | Moves override diagnostics, interface implementation, default conflict checks, and duplicate override checks to shared relation queries. |
| Method implementation resolver + default emission planning integration | 800-1400 | 1.6-2.8 | Selects concrete/default implementations, removes overridden defaults, preserves superclass-selected defaults, defines emission actions, and feeds verifier-safe emission planning. |
| Shared bridge target discovery and descriptor dedup | 450-800 | 0.9-1.6 | Replaces bridge semantic rediscovery with `OverriddenTargets` queries; includes descriptor deduplication and runtime tests. |
| Cleanup, compatibility shims removal, Recheck/cache integration | 300-600 | 0.6-1.2 | Removes old ad-hoc paths, casual `front()` usage, and ensures Recheck clears all new metadata/caches. |
| **Subtotal production C++** | **5200-8650** | **10.4-17.3** | Based strictly on the 500 added C++ LOC = 1 man-month model. |

Additional non-C++ / process effort:

| Work item | Estimated effort | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Test suite expansion | 1.5-3.3 MM | Positive/negative checker tests, runtime dispatch tests, selected default-method dispatch tests, bridge tests, plugin/Recheck cache-safety tests, and generic substitution/viewpoint tests. |
| Diagnostics polish and review iterations | 0.4-0.8 MM | Especially around overload-equivalence, inherited explicit overloads, and interface conflicts. |
| CI/flaky/debugging buffer | 0.3-0.9 MM | Needed because changes touch checker ordering, default-method emission, lowering, and bridges. |

Planning totals:

- **Initial characterization/triage:** roughly **0.5-1.0 MM**, mostly tests, CTS-suppression analysis, and query/API scoping; no separate production patch milestone.
- **Useful MVP** (helpers, shared relation queries, method implementation resolution for common cases, generic view support for common inheritance cases, method overload-set centralization for common calls, explicit overload expansion): roughly **6.8-11.7 MM** plus tests/review buffer.
- **Full migration** to the fully factored oracle-style design: roughly **12.6-22.3 MM** including tests/review/CI buffer.
- **Practical minimum implementation** (one internal relation component, no separate service classes, no epoch/LSP work, no full bridge-phase unification): roughly **8.0-13.0 MM** by the same LOC model, plus tests/review/CI buffer.

---

## Minimum test coverage matrix

| Area | Required tests |
| --- | --- |
| Multiple interfaces | Regression for accepted superclass method implementing two abstract interfaces; concrete superclass method dominating two interface defaults; conflicting defaults without class method; diamond inheritance. |
| Default interface methods | Subinterface default overriding superinterface default; inherited superclass-selected default; multiple unresolved defaults; generic interface defaults after substitution; verifier-safe emitted representation. |
| Override compatibility | Contravariant parameters; covariant returns; access weakening; final method; duplicate override of same base method. |
| Overload-equivalence | Same parameters with different return type; generic erasure collisions; constructor overload-equivalence. |
| Overload order | Textual order; explicit list order; own before superclass before interfaces; `implements`/`extends` order. |
| Explicit overloads | Listed implicit overload group expansion; inherited explicit overload from multiple interfaces; alias same as method name. |
| Generics | Generic class/interface override views; substituted inherited signatures; generic overload candidates; generic bridge dispatch; type-parameter constraint compatibility. |
| Runtime dispatch | Calls through superclass reference; calls through interface reference; selected default interface dispatch; one method overriding several inherited signatures; bridge dispatch. |
| Plugin/LSP cache safety | Recheck after post-check plugin mutation clears relation caches; post-bind plugin mutation does not call checker `Recheck`; optional epoch/generation checks can later catch stale cache reuse. |

---

The migration should be sold and executed as **problem-driven slices**, not as a framework rewrite. A patch may add shared helper infrastructure, but it should land together with an observable frontend bug fix or an unsuppressed regression test.

Rule for each slice:

- name the externally visible problem it fixes;
- add or unsuppress focused tests in the same slice;
- introduce only the shared helper/query code needed for that problem;
- avoid landing generic framework code with no immediate consumer.

Management-facing bug/value map:

| Slice | Frontend problem fixed | Typical proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Characterization | Suppressed overriding failures are hidden and not costed. | Minimal repros + CTS bug-family matrix. |
| Shared override compatibility | Override decisions differ between checker paths and can have side effects such as `SetOverride()`. | Same result for `override` diagnostics, interface checks, and duplicate-override checks. |
| Effective-signature wrappers | Source duplicate/erasure diagnostics depend on assembler strings or raw types. | Overload-equivalence and erasure-collision tests. |
| Explicit overload expansion | Explicit overload declarations can drop/reject implicit overload groups. | Explicit overload list containing `foo` with multiple call signatures. |
| Generic inherited views | Generic base/interface methods are compared as declarations, not as inherited instantiated views. | `D extends B<string>` and generic interface/default tests. |
| Duplicate override detection | Multiple methods overriding the same base method can miss required CTE. | `several_methods_override_negative` family. |
| Concrete implementation dominates defaults | Superclass/class method can be ignored when resolving interface-default conflicts. | `class C2 extends C1 implements I1, I2` default-method regression. |
| Interface default selection | Subinterface defaults and inherited selected defaults are not resolved as one group. | `methods_overriding`, `overriding_public_method`, selected default dispatch. |
| Default emission | Compiler can emit verifier-visible multiple defaults. | Previously classlinker/verifier-failing default tests pass. |
| Method overload-set centralization | Property lookup/synthetic overload variables can lose candidates or order. | Method-call and explicit-overload ordering tests. |
| Bridge target discovery | Generic/override bridge phases can duplicate or miss adapters. | Runtime dispatch through erased/generic base/interface references. |
| Recheck/plugin safety | Cached signatures, calls, overload/default decisions can survive AST mutation. | Recheck/plugin mutation smoke tests. |
| Cleanup | Old divergent paths can reintroduce fixed bugs. | Deleting old predicates does not regress the enabled tests. |

## Phase 10: fix duplicate or missing bridge adapters

Once shared override-query behavior is reliable:

- stop old semantic bridge rediscovery from disagreeing with shared relation queries;
- make bridge code query `OverriddenTargets` for each own concrete method;
- treat generic-substitution bridges and override-conversion bridges as reasons attached to the same override target, not as separate hierarchy searches;
- deduplicate by effective/assembly descriptor;
- preserve existing bridge body generation helpers where possible.

This should be one coherent switch to avoid duplicate or missing bridges. Physical bridge phases may stay split initially; what must become shared is semantic target discovery and descriptor deduplication.

## Phase 11: remove obsolete paths that can reintroduce fixed bugs

This cleanup should also be justified by a bug-prevention argument: old predicates and synthetic lookup paths are alternative semantic implementations, so leaving them active can reintroduce already-fixed behavior when a new call site uses the wrong path.

After migration:

- reduce overload-specific property lookup flags;
- remove or shrink synthetic overload variable construction in `GetProperty`;
- remove duplicated override predicates;
- remove casual `CallSignatures().front()` in overload paths;
- make call resolution consume overload sets directly from shared relation queries.

## What can be done gradually

Safe gradual changes:

1. Add characterization tests.
2. Classify suppressed overriding failures by owning relation query group.
3. Add pure helper functions.
4. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision.
5. Audit `GetApparentType` and add effective-signature wrapper helpers.
6. Introduce one checker-owned `SemanticRelations`/`SemanticRelationCache` component with delegated query helpers.
7. Move method overload-set construction behind the shared relation component where currently needed.
8. Move override diagnostics and interface validation behind shared override queries.
9. Add method implementation resolution behind the same relation component.
10. Remove duplicate predicates after relation consumers are stable.

---

## What should be done all at once

Some changes must be atomic because partial migration would create inconsistent semantics.

| Change | Why it should be atomic |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit overload expansion | Validation, synthetic type construction, call resolution, and lowering must agree about candidate count/order. |
| Resolved call target representation | Checker and lowering must switch together from owner-variable assumptions to explicit target metadata. |
| Shared bridge target discovery switch | Running old semantic rediscovery and new relation-driven target discovery together risks duplicate or missing bridges. |
| Default-method emission switch | Checker implementation-resolution results and emitted/default-forwarding representation must agree, otherwise verifier/linker can still see multiple defaults. |
| Direct overload-set call resolution | `MemberExpression`, `CallExpression`, method references, explicit overloads, and lowering must agree. |
| Effective overload-equivalence across declaration kinds | Functions, methods, interfaces, and constructors must use the same language rule. |

---

## Recommended implementation order

1. Add characterization tests and classify suppressed overriding failures by relation query group.
2. Add pure override compatibility and overload-equivalence helpers.
3. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision checks.
4. Audit `GetApparentType`, add effective-signature wrappers, and use them for overload-equivalence.
5. Add checker-owned `SemanticRelations`/`SemanticRelationCache` with coarse cache clearing; conceptual `OverrideOracle`, `OverloadSetOracle`, method implementation, and generic-view query groups can be implemented as methods/helpers first.
6. Add generic view/substitution support for inherited signatures used by shared relation queries.
7. Implement explicit overload expansion as an atomic patch.
8. Move method overload-set construction into the shared relation component behind existing APIs where currently needed.
9. Migrate interface implementation/conflict checks to shared override and implementation-resolution queries.
10. Add verifier-safe selected-default emission based on implementation-resolution results.
11. Migrate overload-set duplicate suppression to shared override-target queries.
12. Make bridge phases consume shared override-target discovery/dedup; physical bridge-phase unification is optional initially.
13. Remove obsolete synthetic/ad-hoc overload paths.

---

## Recommended problem-driven implementation order

1. Make hidden failures measurable: add characterization tests and classify suppressed overriding failures by relation query group.
2. Fix inconsistent override predicates: add view-based pure `CheckOverrideCompatibility` and migrate one diagnostic path that currently disagrees or has side effects.
3. Fix source overload-equivalence diagnostics: split language overload-equivalence from ABI collision checks.
4. Fix effective-signature duplicate/erasure cases: audit `GetApparentType`, add effective-signature wrappers, and use them for overload-equivalence.
5. Fix explicit overload alias candidate loss: expand implicit overload groups atomically and update validation/type construction/lowering together.
6. Fix generic inherited method views: reuse instantiated supertypes, `ETSObjectType::Substitute`, and `Signature::Substitute` for override/default/overload view signatures.
7. Fix missing duplicate override-of-same-base diagnostics: introduce the minimum `SemanticRelations`/`OverriddenTargets` support needed for that test family.
8. Fix class/superclass implementation dominance over interface defaults: add group-based implementation resolution for the concrete-superclass/default-conflict family.
9. Fix subinterface/default selection: preserve selected inherited defaults and remove overridden superinterface defaults.
10. Fix verifier-visible multiple defaults: make lowering/default emission consume implementation-resolution results.
11. Fix method overload-set candidate loss/order in calls: move the affected method lookup paths behind shared overload-set queries.
12. Fix duplicate/missing bridge adapters: make bridge phases consume shared overridden-target discovery and descriptor deduplication.
13. Fix Recheck/plugin stale-data risks for the new metadata: clear relation/call/default/bridge caches conservatively.
14. Prevent regression: remove obsolete synthetic/ad-hoc overload and override paths once enabled tests no longer depend on them.

CandidateOrigin origin; // own, explicit, superclass, interface size_t sourceOrder; };

A candidate is more than a signature. Lowering needs to know which declaration was selected. Diagnostics may need the origin. Ordering must be stable and spec-derived.

This also avoids guessing selected targets later from Signature::OwnerVar(), which is fragile with synthetic/helper/imported signatures.

Target design

Resolved call target

After overload resolution, the call expression should store both the selected signature and the selected semantic target.

struct ResolvedCallTarget {
    Signature *signature;
    ir::AstNode *declaration;
    varbinder::Variable *variable;
    CallTargetKind kind; // function, instance method, static method, constructor
};

callExpr->SetSignature(target.signature);
callExpr->SetResolvedCallTarget(target);

Checker responsibility

Resolve overloads and choose a target using source-language semantics.

Lowering responsibility

Rewrite syntax according to the already selected target. Do not redo overload resolution.

Updated target design

Shared relation-driven bridge discovery

for (auto derived : OwnConcreteMethodViews(classType)) {
    for (auto target : relations.OverriddenTargets(classType, derived)) {
        if (NeedsBridge(target.base.viewSignature, derived.viewSignature)) {
            GenerateBridge(target.base, derived);
        }
    }
}

This makes bridge planning a mechanical consequence of the same override relation queries used by diagnostics. Physical bridge phases may stay split initially if they share target discovery and descriptor deduplication.

  • Deduplicate bridges by effective or assembly descriptor.
  • Treat generic-substitution and override-conversion bridges as reasons attached to the same override target.
  • Mark generated methods as synthetic/bridge.
  • Exclude bridge methods from source overload sets.
  • Default-method forwarders are planned by default emission, not by bridge discovery.
  • No permanent stored override relation table is required.
Migration plan

Principle: do not rewrite everything at once

The current code is intertwined with many other frontend phases. A total rewrite would be risky. The safe strategy is to introduce better semantic primitives while keeping existing APIs alive, then migrate consumers one by one.

Good gradual changes

Add tests, bug-family triage, helper predicates, checker-owned lazy oracles behind old APIs, and conservative cache clearing on Recheck/plugins.

Atomic changes

Some changes must update checker + lowering together, especially explicit overload expansion and resolved call target representation.

Plugin and LSP note

Short-term safe recompute, long-term incremental API

Plugins may modify AST at defined points in the pipeline. Override-oracle and overload-set caches should therefore be treated as derived semantic data that can be discarded and rebuilt lazily when a plugin mutation barrier is crossed.

Short-term policy

  • After parse: continue normal scope init, binding, and checking.
  • After bind but before check: no checker Recheck is needed, because no check has happened yet. If binding is invalidated, rerun binding and then proceed to the first check.
  • After check: use the safe Recheck path. During that recheck, signatures, override-oracle caches, overload-set caches, implementation-resolution caches, and resolved call targets are cleared and rebuilt lazily.

Long-term optimization

  • Introduce an API to mark what changed: body, call site, method signature, class member set, heritage, explicit overload declaration, etc.
  • Use those marks to recompute override queries and overload sets incrementally where safe.
  • This is useful not only for plugins, but also for LSP support where small edits should avoid full program recheck.

edits.newText:
Principle: every slice fixes a frontend bug

The current code is intertwined with many other frontend phases. A total rewrite would be risky and hard to justify. The safe strategy is to land problem-driven slices: each patch may add shared helpers, but it must also fix or enable a concrete failing behavior.

Good gradual changes

Add tests, bug-family triage, helper predicates, checker-owned lazy relation queries, and conservative cache clearing only when they are tied to an enabled bug-family test.

Atomic changes

Some bug fixes must update checker + lowering together, especially explicit overload expansion, resolved call targets, default emission, and bridge target discovery.

No framework-only milestone: infrastructure should land with the first consumer that fixes an observable frontend problem.

Management view

Problem-driven migration slices

SliceFrontend problem fixed
Shared override compatibilityChecker paths disagree or mutate state while answering override questions.
Effective-signature wrappersSource duplicate/erasure diagnostics depend on assembler strings or raw types.
Explicit overload expansionExplicit overload aliases drop implicit overload groups.
Generic inherited viewsGeneric base/interface methods are compared as declarations, not instantiated views.
Duplicate override detectionSeveral methods can override the same base method without required CTE.
Default implementation resolutionSuperclass methods, subinterface defaults, and inherited selected defaults are not resolved as one group.
Default emissionCompiler can emit verifier-visible conflicting default implementations.
Bridge target discoveryGeneric/override bridge phases can duplicate or miss adapters.
Management view

Patch acceptance rule

1. Name the bug

Each migration slice starts with a concrete frontend failure or suppressed CTS family.

2. Add proof

Land focused tests or unsuppress existing tests in the same slice.

3. Limit infrastructure

Add only the helper/query/cache code needed by that bug fix.

If a helper has no immediate bug-fixing consumer, do not land it yet.

    • Short-term correctness should not depend on plugins providing precise invalidation marks. Conservative recomputation is safer.

    Migration phase 0

    Add characterization tests first

    Before refactoring, write tests that describe both current failures and intended behavior. These tests become the safety net for each later phase.

    AreaTests
    Multiple interfacesRegression for accepted superclass method satisfying two abstract interfaces; concrete superclass method dominating two interface defaults; conflicting defaults without class method.

    Override compatibilityContravariant params, covariant returns, access weakening, final method override, duplicate override of same base.

    Explicit overloadsListed implicit overload group expansion; alias same as method; inherited aliases from multiple interfaces.
    GenericsGeneric class/interface override views; substituted inherited signatures; generic overload candidates; generic bridge dispatch; type-parameter constraint compatibility.
    Runtime dispatchCalls through superclass and interface references; selected default interface dispatch; bridge dispatch; one method overrides several inherited methods.
    Migration phase 1

    Classify suppressed overriding failures

    Do not turn the default-interface example into a one-off patch. The ignored CTS tests show several nearby bug families, so first map each failure to the shared relation query that must own it.

    Bug familyOwning query group
    Duplicate override of same base methodshared override queries
    Class/superclass implementation dominates defaultsoverride queries + implementation resolution
    Subinterface default overrides superinterface defaultimplementation resolution using override dominance
    Generic default/override viewsgeneric-view helpers
    Verifier-safe default emissionimplementation resolution + lowering consumer
    Migration phase 2

    Extract pure semantic helpers

    The next step is to make semantic relations explicit and side-effect-free. A predicate should not mutate the AST or mark a method as overriding while answering a yes/no question.

    OverrideDecision CheckOverrideCompatibility(ETSChecker *checker,
                                            const MethodView &base,
                                            const MethodView &derived);
bool IsOverrideCompatible(ETSChecker *checker,
                          const MethodView &base,
                          const MethodView &derived);
bool AreOverloadEquivalent(Signature *a, Signature *b);
bool IsConcreteImplementationOf(const MethodView &impl,
                                const MethodView &requirement);

    Before

    Compatibility checks can call SetOverride() as a side effect.

    After

    First compute compatibility. Then consumers use the shared relation query result without predicate side effects.

    Migration phase 3

    Separate overload-equivalence from ABI collision

    This is a cleanup with behavior impact. It prevents source-language diagnostics from depending on backend descriptor behavior.

    // Source-language rule
bool AreOverloadEquivalent(Signature *a, Signature *b);

// Backend/helper/bridge rule

// Ambient/helper-specific rule

    Apply the language-level helper consistently to functions, methods, interfaces, and constructors.

    Migration phase 4

    Audit GetApparentType and add wrappers

    Do not create a parallel effective-type representation. Use GetApparentType() as the implementation point, but expose source-semantic wrappers and migrate one consumer at a time.

    1. Audit/fix GetApparentType() against the spec effective-type table.
    2. Add EffectiveType, EffectiveSignatureType, and effective signature key helpers as thin wrappers.
    3. Use them in AreOverloadEquivalent and MethodKey.
    4. Add erasure-collision override diagnostics.
    5. Use them in bridge necessity checks through shared override-target queries.

    Do not spread raw GetApparentType() into ordinary source type-relation checks. Effective signature type and assembler descriptors are related but different semantic layers.

    Migration phase 5

    Atomic explicit overload expansion patch

    This change should be done all at once because validation, type construction, call resolution, and lowering must agree about how many candidates an explicit overload alias has.

    • Allow listed names that resolve to implicit overload groups.
    • Expand all signatures of a listed group in source order.
    • Remove front()-only behavior from explicit overload construction.
    • Store selected target after resolution.
    • Update overload mapping lowering to consume the selected target.

    A partial implementation is dangerous: the checker could resolve to a candidate that lowering cannot correctly rewrite.

    Migration phase 6

    Introduce SemanticRelations and lazy caches

    Add one checker-owned relation component before removing old code. Initially, it can delegate internally to existing helpers while adding a common API, cache clearing, and debug tracing. Epoch/generation checks are optional and can be added later.

    checker->SemanticRelations().IsOverride(...);
checker->SemanticRelations().OverriddenTargets(...);
checker->SemanticRelations().ResolveInterfaceImplementation(...);
checker->SemanticRelations().GetMethodOverloadSet(...);
checker->SemanticRelations().ViewSignature(...);
    • Override queries answer override and implementation questions.
    • Method overload-set queries build candidate lists on demand.
    • Implementation-resolution queries select concrete/default method implementations.
    • Generic-view helpers provide substituted inherited signature views.
    • All caches are valid only until the next explicit cache clear.
    Migration phase 7

    Move method overload-set construction behind shared queries

    Do not immediately delete synthetic property lookup behavior. Instead, make it delegate to the shared relation component first.

    ETSObjectType::CreateSyntheticVarFromEverySignature(...) {
    auto set = checker->SemanticRelations().GetMethodOverloadSet(...);
    return CreateSyntheticFunctionTypeFrom(set);
}

    This lets existing call sites keep working while method overload set formation becomes centralized, cached, and testable.

    Migration phase 8

    Migrate override consumers to shared override queries

    No permanent override state is required. Each validation pass asks the shared relation component the exhaustive questions it needs; the component caches answers.

    1. Use it for override keyword diagnostics.
    2. Use it for final/access/return diagnostics.
    3. Use it for duplicate override-of-same-base detection.
    4. Use it for interface implementation and conflict validation.
    5. Use it for inherited overload candidate suppression.
    Migration phase 9

    Method implementation resolution

    After interface validation uses shared override queries, add one default-method resolution path and make checker diagnostics agree with emitted/default-forwarding representation.

    • Collect applicable interface defaults for a class/method key.
    • Remove defaults overridden by more specific subinterface defaults.
    • Prefer concrete class/superclass implementations when present.
    • Preserve superclass-selected defaults as inherited implementations.
    • Use substituted generic interface views.
    • Prevent verifier-visible unresolved multiple defaults.
    Migration phase 10

    Bridge phases consume shared target discovery

    Once shared override queries are stable, bridge planning should stop rediscovering overrides independently and query shared overridden-target discovery instead.

    • Both current bridge phases may remain physically separate at first.
    • They should consume the same overridden-target facts.
    • Treat generic-substitution and override-conversion needs as reasons on the same target.
    • Deduplicate by effective/assembly descriptor.
    • Reuse bridge body builders where possible.
    • Add runtime dispatch tests for generated bridges.

    Running old semantic rediscovery beside new target discovery risks duplicate bridge methods or inconsistent signatures; physical phase unification is optional, but shared semantics are not.

    Gradual vs atomic

    What can be done gradually

    • Add characterization tests.
    • Add pure semantic helpers.
    • Classify suppressed overriding failures by owning semantic service.
    • Split source overload-equivalence from ABI collision helpers.
    • Audit GetApparentType and add effective-signature wrapper helpers.
    • Introduce one checker-owned SemanticRelations/SemanticRelationCache component.
    • Move method overload-set construction behind shared relation queries where currently needed.
    • Migrate diagnostics and validations one by one to shared override queries.
    • Add method implementation resolution behind the same relation component.
    • Clean up obsolete helper paths after replacement.
    Gradual vs atomic

    What should be done all at once

Explicit overload group expansionChecker, synthetic type construction, call resolution, and lowering must agree on candidate count and order. Resolved call target representationChecker and lowering must switch together, otherwise lowering will keep relying on fragile owner-variable assumptions. Shared bridge target discovery switchOld semantic rediscovery and new relation-driven target discovery running together can create duplicate or missing bridge methods. Default-method emission switchChecker implementation-resolution results and emitted/default-forwarding representation must agree, otherwise verifier/linker can still see multiple defaults. Direct overload-set call resolutionMember expressions, call expressions, method references, and explicit overload aliases must share the same candidate source. Global effective overload-equivalenceFunctions, methods, constructors, and interfaces must follow the same source-language duplicate rule.
Recommended order

Practical implementation sequence

  1. Add characterization tests and classify suppressed overriding failures by semantic service.
  2. Add pure override compatibility and overload-equivalence helpers.
  3. Split overload-equivalence from ABI collision logic.
  4. Audit GetApparentType, add effective-signature wrappers, and use them for overload-equivalence.
  5. Add checker-owned SemanticRelations/SemanticRelationCache with conceptual override, overload, implementation, and generic-view query groups.
  6. Add generic view/substitution support for inherited signatures used by shared relation queries.
  7. Implement explicit overload group expansion as an atomic patch.
  8. Move method overload-set construction into the shared relation component behind existing APIs where currently needed.
  9. Migrate interface implementation/conflict checks to shared override and implementation-resolution queries.
  10. Add verifier-safe selected-default emission based on implementation-resolution results.
  11. Migrate overload-set inherited duplicate suppression to shared override-target queries.
  12. Make bridge phases consume shared override-target discovery/dedup; physical bridge-phase unification is optional initially.
  13. Remove old ad-hoc/synthetic overload paths where no longer needed.
Workload estimation

Planning model and caveats

For planning, use the requested model: 500 added C++ production lines ≈ 1 man-month.

What the model captures

  • new checker/relation/lowering C++ code;
  • new helper types and cache APIs;
  • integration code for Recheck/cache clearing.

What it undercounts

  • tests and diagnostics text;
  • review iterations and CI debugging;
  • large refactors with low net added lines;
  • flaky/runtime bridge investigation.

Ranges below are broad. The implementation touches checker, object type lookup, explicit overload validation, default-method resolution/emission, lowering, bridge generation, and Recheck cleanup.

  1. Make hidden failures measurable: characterize and classify suppressed overriding failures.
  2. Fix inconsistent override predicates with view-based CheckOverrideCompatibility.
  3. Fix source overload-equivalence diagnostics by separating ABI collision logic.
  4. Fix effective-signature duplicate/erasure cases through GetApparentType wrappers.
  5. Fix explicit overload alias candidate loss with atomic group expansion.
  6. Fix generic inherited method views using existing instantiated supertype/substitution machinery.
